rationale: A ratio between 0.9 and 1.5 means most of the deposits are lent out. It is unusual for this sector and a supervisor should ask why.
A ratio above 1.5 means the institution has lent out more than it holds in deposits. The funding position is the priority.
An institution that reports no deposits either stopped operating or submitted an incomplete return. Either way it cannot be supervised from this record.

message: Institution holds a large share of sector deposits
rationale: A single institution holding more than a quarter of reported sector deposits is a concentration risk for the sector as a whole.

message: Deposits fell sharply against the previous period
rationale: A fall of more than 20% in deposits against the previous period is a run signal. It needs a supervisor before the next filing.

message: Loans grew by more than 50% against the previous period
rationale: Fast loan growth changes the risk profile of a book. It is worth a look even when the level is normal.
When the whole sector lends more than it holds, the sector depends on wholesale or interbank funding to keep running.

message: Sector deposit market is moderately concentrated
rationale: An index above 2000 is the conventional entry point for a moderately concentrated market. A supervisor should know how concentrated the sector it supervises is.
An institution under enhanced monitoring that has filed a curated record belongs on the supervisor's desk, whatever its numbers look like.

message: Fewer than 80% of expected institutions reported
rationale: Low coverage means the sector picture is incomplete. Any sector number computed on it is incomplete too.
